speaker: V. A. Kazakov
title: Planar maps, matrix integrals, and two-dimensional gravity
summary: The catalogue range overlaps Ginzburg and Ovsienko. Kazakov actually begins in the lower part of P001298 and continues through P001302: triangulated spheres, the cubic Hermitian matrix model, its planar expansion, eigenvalue saddle, and critical exponent. The formal combinatorial integral must be distinguished from a convergent integral over real Hermitian matrices. Record 695 revisits the counting conventions.

speaker: V. Yu. Ovsienko
title: KdV and super-KdV as Euler equations
summary: The mathematical report occupies only the middle of P001298, between Ginzburg\textquotesingle s Hecke-algebra discussion and Kazakov\textquotesingle s random surfaces. It identifies KdV and its supersymmetric extensions with Euler equations for Virasoro-type groups; the catalogue\textquotesingle s wide page range does not transfer adjacent talks to Ovsienko.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg
title: Generalized Lie algebras: manuscript attribution to D. Gurevich
summary: The catalogue identifies Ginzburg on 29 September. The original heading on P001303 instead reads D. Gurevich, 13 October 1986, followed by generalized Lie algebras and groups. We retain the catalogue record but attribute the surviving mathematical items explicitly to D. I. Gurevich. They concern involutive Yang--Baxter operators, braided Lie identities, super and color examples, and braided commutators. Kazakov begins later on P001304.

speaker: V. A. Kazakov
title: Ising spins on random triangulations and Wick expansion
summary: The catalogue date is preserved, but this exposition begins after the Gurevich heading dated 13 October and occupies P001304--P001306. It introduces annealed Ising gravity, a two-matrix representation, a critical temperature, and a Wick-theorem intervention by A. N. Varchenko. Ginzburg\textquotesingle s braid discussion starts with the next dated heading and is not part of this record.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg
title: Polynomial monodromy and the Burau representation
summary: The actual mathematical section is P001307--P001308. It constructs braid representations from cohomology of a punctured plane, identifies a Hecke relation, and asks faithfulness of Burau. The same letter is used for an exponent and a multiplicative monodromy parameter; the hyperelliptic example makes the ambiguity substantive.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: The Deligne--Illusie proof of Hodge degeneration
summary: The short report at the top of P001309 announces an algebraic proof of degeneration of the Hodge--de Rham spectral sequence, referring to an Orsay preprint by Deligne and Illusie. The theorem over characteristic zero and the new positive-characteristic method are separate items.

speaker: V. A. Kazakov
title: Unitary orbital integrals and reduced gauge models
summary: The section from the lower part of P001309 through P001311 develops the Harish-Chandra--Itzykson--Zuber integral, recalls the principal-minor spherical-function formula, and explains the radial heat operator. It closes with a two-source integral and the Eguchi--Kawai matrix reduction. The final assertion that the reduced integral contains all gauge theory needs a center-symmetry qualification.

speaker: I. S. Zakharevich
title: Orbital integration, interlacing, and concentration remarks
summary: The new dated heading begins at P001312. The report revisits the orbital-integral heat proof and the spectral distribution of products of positive matrices, then uses sections of ellipsoids and interlacing arrays. Gelfand adds two high-dimensional intuition questions. Their printed numerical and dynamical assertions require separate qualifications.

speaker: B. V. Lidskii
title: The diagonal moment map
summary: The short intervention occupies the middle of P001313. It identifies the diagonal projection on a unitary orbit as a moment map and relates its Fourier transform to the orbital integral. The uncertain handwritten initial is not used to override the catalogue identification. Gelfand\textquotesingle s question about a super analogue of the symmetric group follows.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg
title: Exact stationary phase and localization
summary: The lower part of P001313 gives an approximate Duistermaat--Heckman formula, its coadjoint-orbit example, and Gelfand\textquotesingle s questions about higher asymptotic terms and characteristic numbers. A final conjectural sentence is explicitly marked mine by the note-taker; it must not be attributed to Gelfand or Ginzburg.

speaker: G. I. Olshanskii
title: Spherical functions behind principal-minor integrals
summary: The actual exposition begins on P001314 and ends in the upper part of P001315. Olshanskii explains the Gelfand--Naimark formula through highest-weight characters and spherical functions, with HCIZ as a limiting form. Gelfand asks which other integrals admit such an interpretation.

speaker: V. G. Drinfeld
title: Quantizing KdV and the second Gelfand--Dickey bracket
summary: The section actually runs from the lower part of P001315 through P001318. It distinguishes the compatible KdV brackets, their free-field and Miura realizations, higher-order operators, and quantum commuting integrals. Gelfand and Feigin intervene. Three final questions concern quantization of KdV integrals, their spectrum in irreducible Virasoro representations, and general second-bracket quantization. The spectral question receives a bounded level-two development in this chapter; P001319 instead begins Beilinson on 10 November.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Virasoro uniformization and differential equations on moduli of curves
summary: The catalogue gives no page range, but the original P001319 heading clearly names Beilinson and 10 November 1986. The coherent continuation P001319--P001321 supplies surviving notes: formal-coordinate uniformization of pointed curves, determinant-line twists, and differential equations obtained from singular Virasoro vectors. This attribution is an explicit editorial recovery from the manuscript; the empty catalogue page field is retained. The note credits Kontsevich and Beilinson--Schechtman independently and refers to Belavin through Drinfeld.

speaker: V. A. Kazakov
title: Random surfaces, Gaussian embeddings, and coupled matrix integrals
summary: The actual section is P001322--P001325, jointly headed Kazakov and Zakharevich; interventions by Gelfand are marked. It compares the bosonic-string action with triangulated Gaussian surfaces, revisits weighted planar-map counting, and presents a two-source unitary integral and three-state matrix model. The final three- and four-dimensional gauge question repeats record 688. The lattice-theory report beginning P001326 belongs to record 696.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Subspace configurations and preprojective reductions of modular lattices
summary: The manuscript section P001326--P001327 names a joint project with B. V. Lidskii and V. A. Ponomarev. It reviews subspace configurations and the free modular lattice, distinguishes word equality from linear equivalence, and announces a preprojective quotient and perfect elements. The printed 1987 paper supplies necessary restrictions omitted in the notebook. Finite axiomatizability, decidability, and classification of representations are different questions.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: The unitary dual of general linear groups
summary: The talk begins on P001328 and ends at the top of P001330, before Kazakov. It reports the unitary-dual classification of Tadić and Vogan through determinant characters, complementary series, and normalized parabolic induction, then discusses square-integrable building blocks over local fields. Gelfand adds a kernel model for invariant Hermitian forms. The main formulas are recoverable, but the absolute-value normalization, modular character, center quotient, and segment exponents need correction or qualification.
